Theme

School & learning

essay noun

also essays, composition, school essay, paper, write a composition, theme (essay), write a theme

classical

Cic. Brut. 92: nūlla enim rēs tantum ad dīcendum prōficit quantum scrīptiō
Cic. Tusc. 5.121: philosophiae scrīptiōnēs (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. composition, paper (school), after Egger

scrīptiō, scrīptiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a written composition, an essay

Composition in writing, Cicero’s exercise for the orator, and in the plural written works; Egger uses it of a paper written at school (Morgan–Owens). The subject set is the thema or argūmentum (see subject, a topic).

Other words

  • commentātiō, commentātiōnis f. — a written study, a paper

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 8.44 (Lewis & Short); Gell. praef. 4

    Classically careful preparation, then a written study (the elder Pliny, Gellius); see also article.

  • tractātus, tractātūs m. — an essay, a treatise

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Traupman 32, 310, 393; Plin. NH 14.45: tōtō tractātū (Lewis & Short)

    A handling of a subject (Quintilian), a treatise in the elder Pliny; Traupman’s word for an essay, beside libellus (p. 29).

  • scrīptūra, scrīptūrae f. — a writing, a composition

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.150: assidua ac dīligēns scrīptūra (Lewis & Short); Traupman 25, 28; Traupman 294

    Lewis & Short: “a writing, composing, composition”.

  • compositiō, compositiōnis f. — a composition (school essay)

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 25, 28; Traupman 294

    Classically the putting together of things, and in rhetoric the arrangement of words (Lewis & Short); the school sense is modern.

  • libellus, libellī m. — a little book, a short piece of writing

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 29

    The diminutive of liber: a booklet, a pamphlet, a short written piece (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nūlla enim rēs tantum ad dīcendum prōficit quantum scrīptiō

    for nothing does so much for speaking as writing compositionsCic. Brut. 92

  • Crās tibi trādenda est scrīptiō dē Bulgariā.

    You have to hand in an essay on Bulgaria tomorrow.composed

  • tractātum cōnscrībere

    to write a themeTraupman 393

See also subject, article, write, homework, author.
